changelog: v347: an introduction names one person in one clause, and a name the vault has already placed in the family keeps its place. WHERE IT WAS SEEN: v346's rule 2 — a relationship phrase introduces a person — shipped on 2026-09-24 and was run against the owner's vault the same day. `entity-roster --ensure-introduced --dry-run` proposed four people and one of them was his paternal GRANDFATHER filed as a second father: `desiree-taylor` (parent, from "mom", born 1955-06-19) correct; `katie-taylor` (spouse, from "wife", born 1987-05-15) correct; `james-taylor` (parent, from "dad") the right man; and `james-edwin-taylor-sr` — James Edwin Taylor **Sr.**, born 1930-10-17, the owner's paternal grandfather — also `parent`, also "from dad". The reading came out of one evidence quote on `claim:e18ea8f6edc28fd649a133c3` (`resolver:59031241b7130db1fa6a6696`), which says the opposite of what was read out of it: "story: my grandpa James Edwin Taylor Sr., my dad's dad, died of a heart attack". v346's appositive shape `<Name>, <possessive> <word>` matched the name against the "dad" of *my dad's* dad — a relationship word that POSSESSES the next noun, read as though it were the name's own relation — while *grandpa*, the word actually in apposition with the name, went unread. Then v346's own shared-alias rule made it worse in exactly the way it was designed to prevent a different harm: two people claimed "dad", so dad/my dad/father/my father were dropped from BOTH rows, and the owner's real father — James Edwin Taylor, d. 2019, whose own introduction is `sources/manual/2026-08-24-i-think-we-ve-already-talked-about-him-but.md` ("the biggest loss of my life so far is my dad, James Edwin Taylor") — ended up with no relationship word at all. The vault had already said who Sr was, twice, and neither statement was asked: the correction `correction:temporal-4eb9abe8c4ca47089ae83a56` ("these are the owner's grandfathers' births, not his: … James Edwin Taylor Sr (born 1930-10-17) and Darvin Burrows Beauchamp (born 1929-09-30)"), and the last token of the man's own name. THE RULES, all four of them NARROWING v346 rather than widening it — every shape it read before it still reads, and the ones it may not read are named. (1) AN INTRODUCTION NAMES ONE PERSON IN ONE CLAUSE (`roster_relations.AN_INTRODUCTION_NAMES_ONE_PERSON_IN_ONE_CLAUSE`, applied by the new `relationship_phrase_match`, which `relationship_phrase` is now the word half of): the phrase and the name must sit in the SAME clause — `introduction_clauses` splits on `INTRODUCTION_CLAUSE_SEPARATORS` (a newline, the `|` an evidence quote joins its fragments with, `;`, `:`, an em/en dash) and on a sentence end that is not an abbreviation's full stop, so "James Edwin Taylor Sr." and "A.J." are one clause and not two. Inside that clause a relationship word carrying a possessive `'s` is a POSSESSOR and not the name's relation (`_NOT_A_POSSESSOR`, one lookahead carried by both shapes), so "my dad's dad" introduces nobody as a father; a clause that gives one name two different relationships states neither and the next clause is read instead; and the in-law reading (`axis_membership.IN_LAW_RE`) is taken over THAT clause rather than over every text in the source, because "in-law" somewhere else in a conversation says nothing about this name. A name that a pasted vital record merely LISTS is introduced by nothing (`introduces_only_a_pasted_record`, `pasted_record_names`): the genealogy-app shape the owner drops into a card conversation — `Name • 8 Sources` and the man on the next line — read through `landmark_projection.BIRTH_NAME_LINE_RE`, which is already the one definition of it, so no second pattern exists. A relationship word in the surrounding conversation may not reach into somebody else's document. (2) A RECORDED RELATION OUTRANKS AN INTRODUCED ONE (`A_RECORDED_RELATION_OUTRANKS_AN_INTRODUCED_ONE`, `recorded_relation` over `RECORDED_RELATION_TIERS`): before writing, the rule asks what the vault already says about that spelling — a temporal correction's own words, a `family` landmark entry's `relation` (read off `landmark_projection.load_landmark_sources`, the filed records, never the `state/landmarks.json` drawing), a roster row's `relationship`. A recorded relation that AGREES confirms the row (`relationship_basis: "recorded"`); one that CONTRADICTS it refuses the whole row and returns a finding naming both, printed by the CLI, because a vault that has already placed somebody is not corrected by a sentence that reads them differently. The correction tier (`stated_relation`) counts a text only when it names the person — whole-token through `identity_resolution.normalized_mention_key`, never a raw substring — and states EXACTLY ONE relationship, and only when the texts that qualify agree: it exists to CONFIRM or REFUSE an introduction, never to invent one, which is why the owner's own "1990-03-20 is AJ's birthday, not James's … the owner's brother Anthon James 'AJ' Taylor" correction is declined rather than half-read. (3) A GENERATIONAL SUFFIX IS A GENERATION (`GENERATIONAL_SUFFIX_STEPS` stepping along `GENERATION_TIERS`): when the vault holds both `<Name>` and `<Name> Sr.`/`Sr`/`Senior`/`I`, the suffixed one is one generation UP, and `<Name> Jr.`/`Junior` one down, unless a source says otherwise — rule 2 is asked first. `focus_candidate.FOCUS_RELATIONSHIPS` is the gate, so a step onto a seat this roster does not have (a great-grandparent, a grandchild) refuses instead of filing one; `sibling` is the seat for a person of the owner's own generation, because the owner himself is never an introduced row; a shifted row drops the relationship aliases the old word licensed, since a word of the wrong generation must not bind to the person it was the wrong generation for; and the base name is compared WHOLE — "James Taylor" and "James Edwin Taylor" are two spellings this rule deliberately does not join, because four people on the owner's roster bear the token *James* and collapsing a middle name would put his father, his brother and his son in one bucket. On the owner's vault it is rules 1 and 2 that decide Sr, for exactly that reason. (4) A BIRTHDAY SAID WITH THE WORD IS SAID WITH THE NAME: `_introduced_birth` reads v346's `landmark_projection.birth_event_subject` first and then v345's `landmark_projection.names_a_birth` against any spelling the introduction itself licensed, inside the one source that introduced the person. The owner typed "James Taylor my dad was born on June 4th 1954" and the extractor filed the event as "Dad's birthdate recorded", whose tail is not a birth noun; one clause, one person, and the word is the name, so his father's row now carries his 1954-06-04 and the age arithmetic has a birth to measure from. `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` takes `timeline-rules:16`. The arithmetic in `temporal_timeline` did not change: the ROSTER it reads did, and this release is what changes it, so the same claims calculate to a different subject set, a different axis membership and a different age-anchor set for claims nobody edited. RE-RUN on a scratch clone of the owner's vault (`2b15c1c0`), three times: v346 bytes as they stand (generation 152, 1188 nodes, 1158 placed, 38 open cards), v346 bytes plus `--ensure-introduced`, and these bytes plus `--ensure-introduced`. The dry run now proposes exactly four people: `desiree-taylor` (parent, born 1955-06-19, aliases Desi/mom/my mom/mother/my mother), `james-taylor` (parent, born 1954-06-04, aliases James Taylor (Dad)/dad/my dad/father/my father), `katie-taylor` (spouse, born 1987-05-15, aliases wife/my wife) and `james-edwin-taylor-sr` — GRANDPARENT, from "grandpa", `relationship_basis: "recorded"` because the correction agrees, aliases grandfather/my grandfather/grandpa/my grandpa — with no contested alias anywhere and no finding. AGAINST v346 WITH THE SAME WRITER RUN, which is this release's own contribution: fourteen nodes gain the owner's father as a resolved subject where "Dad", "father" and "Father" had named nobody — "Father's near-death and death" (`node:363cb750d87204d306a7618d`, 2020-03/2020-06 stated, three tellings, now `Dave's father` + `person/james-taylor` + `the narrator's father` and `family`/`immediate_family_in_lifetime` instead of `owner`/`lived`), "Dad's move to Irvine", "Dad shatters knee playing basketball", "Father lost his job", "Father's truck foreclosure", "Father's earlier stroke and paralysis", "Dad getting sick", "Dad's illness", "Father got sick", "Dad's frustrated moment at Horse Pools house", two "Dad's graduation" nodes and "Dad wins pet snake at fair". Eleven of them move off the owner's own axis onto his family's, and one moves the other way for the right reason: "Dad wins pet snake at fair" (`node:55b4d58109978a433c069fbe`) is newly PLACED at 1959~ on an age band measured from his father's own 1954-06-04 birth, which is before the owner was born, so it reads `none`/`pre_birth` — rule 4 of the axis ruling, unchanged. Its `precision_gap` card closes: open cards 38 → 37 (`precision_gap` 30 → 29, `contradiction` 7 → 7, `identity_uncertain` 1 → 1), placed 1159 → 1160, 0 dated moments moved, 0 nodes added or removed. "Father's mission to New Zealand" (`node:80f419115b858c37a7b051f3`, 1973-06/1976-06) is byte-identical and still carries the unresolved mention `James Edwin Taylor`: that THIRD spelling of his father is deliberately not introduced, because the shape it arrives in — "my dad, James Edwin Taylor" — is a possessive-then-comma apposition v346 never read, and reading it here would hand "dad" back to nobody by giving it a third claimant. The owner's own birth anchor is still the single 1981-07-11 (`node:f438507de8c274a785692e8f`, stated, `conflict_state: none`) and his five age frames are byte-identical. Measured against the vault AS IT STANDS (v346 bytes, nobody introduced yet), which is what the owner will actually see: nodes 1188 → 1189, placed 1158 → 1160, open cards 38 → 37, fifty nodes' subjects resolve, 43 move from `owner`/`lived` to `family`/`immediate_family_in_lifetime` and 2 to `none`/`pre_birth`, and "Mom married dad at 21" is newly placed at 1976~ off his mother's own birthday. KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE, both of them v346's own documented seam rather than new: adding a roster row re-keys a node whose subject newly resolves and whose claims carry no `event_ref` of their own, because a node id is derived from its subject — "Dad graduated" moves from `node:1bdbc9ecc7305d5a90c6e4a4` to `node:2156ca1018344c8248882c44` with the same label, the same 1987, the same axis and no `node_aliases` redirect, and an undated second "Mom babysat Kodi and Acey Nixon" appears on both the v346 and the v347 run. v342's `node_aliases` covers a BINDER re-key, not an identity one; that is the binder's seam, not the fold's. And the father's DEATH is in the vault — "not Dad James Edwin d.2019" — but under a different spelling and in a different source (the family-birthdays roster, which is Katie's introduction, not his), so his row ships without a `died`: filing it would be the cross-source, cross-spelling identity guess this release exists to refuse. GUARDS: `tests/test_v347_an_introduction_names_one_relation.py` (36 tests) — the quote that made a grandfather a father, reading `grandpa` out of the clause it is actually in; the possessive chain refused with its own control still reading "dad"; a phrase refused across a full stop, a `|`, a `;` and a newline; a name that is not two clauses ("James Edwin Taylor Sr.", "A.J."); one clause that says two relations saying neither; the in-law reading clause-local, with an in-law phrase elsewhere in the source no longer demoting the mother; every shape v346 read still read; the owner's own paste, `pasted_record_names` against `BIRTH_NAME_LINE_RE`, the refusal, and the control where he also says the name himself; the correction the vault already held, the mixed correction declining to read, every tier in order and the tier constant; a contradicted introduction refused with the finding naming both; the suffix table, one generation up and one down, a step off the ladder refusing, the middle name not collapsed, and a shifted row dropping the word of the wrong generation; the whole four-person batch with "dad" bound to the father and the grandfather's pasted birthday not riding along; v346's genuine two-claimant tie still binding to neither; and the writer seat on a synthetic vault with a correction filed through `temporal_store.file_temporal_correction` and read back through `load_temporal_corrections` — no second reader — including a refusal that is reported and not written, a dry run that writes nothing and a second run that converges. The `timeline-rules:16` pins and `tests/goldens/cert_10_place_containment.json` move with the constant. Docs: ADR 0037 gains its v347 amendment (items 21–24), the eras handbook its rule-version row. Ruff parity held: no new rule class on any touched file.
